newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST-Ahmsa full yr seen solid-analysts.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Ahmsa full yr seen solid-analysts.

text.p: Steel maker Altos Hornos de Mexico (Ahmsa) will suffer a setback in the fourth quarter due to one-off events, but the full 1996 year should show improved earnings compared with 1995, analysts said.
A Reuters survey of analysts estimated average 1996 earnings per share of 8.56 pesos. In 1995, earnings per share were 3.12 pesos.
"A couple one-time events should have an impact on earnings, otherwise I expect similar operating margins as the third quarter," Abaco brokerage analyst Bond Snodgrass said.

A sudden spike in energy prices -- which should be brought under control when the company secures its own energy sources -- and losses caused by temporary shut-downs to improve facilities were the main reasons for the loss, analysts said.

Ahmsa reported net profit of 484.77 million pesos in 1995, a reversal from a loss of 2.056 billion pesos in 1994. For the first three quarters of 1996, the company reported net profits of 3.114 billion pesos, up from 1.16 billion in the same period in 1995.
Sandra Morfin of Caspian Securities, citing the peso's weakness and higher energy costs, said the fourth quarter's earnings should register a loss of four centavos per share.

Analysts agreed that natural gas prices, now at a five-year high, will shrink margins. They said the company will remain vulnerable to energy costs until it gets its own energy generating plants on line.
Mexico's natural gas prices averaged about $3.73 per million British Thermal Units (BTU) in December.
But the analysts disagreed on whether or not the company can guarantee a healthier 1997.
"We believe that margins should be weaker than 1996 in 1997 because the real appreciation of the peso will offset the advantage of higher domestic sales," Morfin said.
"Also the company is going to be doing some investments that will require downtime to modernize facilities."
But other analysts said margins should grow next year because there is room to improve and also because of ambitious investment projects.
"We expect the strong investment programs to begin to bear fruit a little after the second quarter," BBV-Probursa analyst Jose Buendia said.
An expected recovery in steel prices later in the year and a shift toward more value-added products, such as coated steel and more flat products, could help Ahmsa's margins in 1997.
"We think that the company has one important advantage in fairly low-cost operations and a lot of upside in terms of efficiency and cost-cutting," Salomon Brothers analyst Mauricio Reveco said.
Reveco estimated that national demand for steel will grow faster than gross domestic product in 1997, as a recovering economy spurs construction.
